final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package: Canada opens dairy at 3.5% quota, labor enforcement is automatic and symmetric (wage floor indexed to Mexico's minimum, quarterly audits, 15% tariff trigger), 75% RVC applies to new model launches month 13 with 24-month grandfathering for existing tooling, Chapter 19 preserved, Friday signature locked. The deal closes before Congressional recess.
minority_objections: Supply-chain manufacturers initially resisted immediate 75% RVC compliance without phase-in clarity, warning of sourcing shifts outside North America
Canada initially refused dairy concessions without binding labor text in hand, threatening to walk rather than join on promises
key_conflicts: Canada vs. U.S./Mexico: dairy opening (3.5% quota) as entry price for trilateral participation
Auto industry vs. USTR: grandfathering window definition—whether 'existing tooling' covers design-phase equipment or only installed lines
Labor union vs. all parties: enforcement mechanism must be automatic with no secretariat discretion, or ratification fails
Supply-chain vs. USTR: phase-in timeline ambiguity (day-one vs. new-launch compliance) threatened to freeze capex investment
key_concessions: Canada: opened dairy at 3.5% quota after securing binding labor text and auto grandfathering clarity
U.S.: preserved Chapter 19 dispute settlement (Canadian red line) and accepted symmetric labor enforcement applying to all three countries
Mexico: committed binding labor text (wage floor indexed to official minimum, quarterly audits, automatic 15% tariff trigger) in writing same-day
USTR: granted 12-month RVC phase-in with 24-month grandfathering for existing tooling (new launches only after month 13)
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement non-negotiable; dairy opening contingent on binding labor enforcement text in writing
Labor union: automatic tariff trigger (no secretariat discretion) required for ratification support
Supply-chain manufacturers: grandfathering definition must lock at signature date or investment freezes
Congress: binding labor text and Friday signature deadline required to hold pre-recess ratification vote
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Sunset clause: mentioned once (R1 supply_chain_mfr proposed review-mechanism compromise) but never resolved—remains a business-uncertainty variable post-signature
Tooling audit disputes: 30-day post-signature window for equipment classification disputes could reopen auto chapter conflicts in month 12
Dairy sector domestic backlash: U.S. dairy industry's political reaction to Canada's 3.5% quota concession not discussed, but USTR accepted ratification risk increase
Mexico's labor law implementation capacity: binding text assumes quarterly audit infrastructure exists, but no discussion of Mexican institutional readiness
downstream_risk_variables: Congressional ratification timeline: Friday signature locks pre-recess vote window, but any delay past recess pushes ratification to October with higher political risk
Tooling classification disputes: month 12 audit panel could surface auto industry objections if 'existing tooling' definitions prove ambiguous in practice
Mexican labor enforcement compliance: automatic tariff trigger depends on quarterly audit capacity and political will to enforce wage floors
Sunset clause unresolved: business investment decisions remain constrained by lack of long-term certainty beyond initial term
uncertainty_notes: Sunset clause never addressed after R1 mention—remains unresolved as a long-term investment constraint. Tooling audit process (30-day post-signature window) could surface disputes in month 12 if equipment classifications prove contentious. Mexican labor law implementation capacity assumed but not verified. U.S. dairy sector domestic ratification risk acknowledged (us_ratification_risk rose +3 in R6) but not mitigated.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC phase-in timeline and 'existing tooling' grandfathering definition drove R3-R7 negotiations; USTR's R6 commitment to month-13 trigger + 24-month window was the concrete proposal that unlocked Canada's dairy concession
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Automatic 15% tariff trigger (no secretariat discretion) was labor union's stated ratification requirement (R3, R6); Mexico's binding text commitment (R3) and USTR's enforcement clarity (R2) were the specific concessions that secured Congressional and labor support
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Canada's 3.5% dairy quota opening was the explicit entry price for trilateral participation (R4 USTR ultimatum, R7 Canada commitment); dairy concession was Canada's final move after securing labor text and auto grandfathering
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Chapter 19 mentioned as Canadian red line (R1, R2) and preserved in final package (R7), but did not drive any specific proposal or concession—acknowledged and set aside
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Mentioned once by supply_chain_mfr in R1 as a review-mechanism alternative to hard sunset, but never discussed again—no follow-up, no proposal, no impact on outcome
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congressional recess deadline drove Friday signature lock (R7 USTR); labor union's automatic-trigger requirement (R3, R6) and Congress's binding-text demand (R2, R5) were stated ratification constraints that shaped enforcement language and timeline
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Supply-chain manufacturers raised capex freeze risk (R1, R4) and tooling classification concerns (R6, R7), but these were addressed via grandfathering language—raised as constraint, resolved via concession, did not block outcome
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: U.S.-Mexico bilateral baseline presented as ultimatum (R1 USTR, R4 Mexico); Canada faced explicit 'join or be excluded' pressure (R4 USTR, R6 Mexico)—this leverage drove Canada's dairy concession in R7
